chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Ṭabarī narrated, he said:
A man from the merchants of Fāris, from among the mawālī of Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, wrote to him asking his permission regarding the khums.
So he wrote back to him: In the Name of Allah, the All-Merciful, the Ever-Merciful.

Indeed Allah is All-Encompassing, Generous. He has guaranteed reward for obedience and punishment for مخالفة. No wealth is lawful except by a means that Allah has made lawful. Indeed khums is our support for our religion, for our dependents, for our mawālī, and for what we ransom and purchase of our honor from those whose assault we fear. So do not withhold it from us, and do not deprive yourselves of our du'a as long as you are able to give it. For indeed paying it is the key to your sustenance, the purification of your sins, and what you send ahead for yourselves for the day of your need. And the Muslim is the one who fulfills to Allah what he has covenanted upon, and the Muslim is not the one who answers with the tongue while opposing with the heart.

key_terms.الْخُمُسَ: the one-fifth due, described here as support for religious and communal obligations
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمُ: the true Muslim, defined here by inward and outward fidelity
key_terms.تَمْحِيصُ ذُنُوبِكُمْ: the cleansing or purifying of your sins
key_terms.دُعَاءَنَا: our du'a, meaning the supplication of the Imam عليه السلام and the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.عَاهَدَ: entered into covenant or pledged, referring to one’s commitment before Allah
key_terms.مَالٌ: wealth or property, which is only lawful through divinely permitted means
key_terms.مِفْتَاحُ رِزْقِكُمْ: the key to your sustenance, indicating barakah connected to giving khums

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Istibṣār say about the obligation and wisdom of paying khums?
ai.summary: This report contains a written reply concerning khums, emphasizing that wealth is only lawful through what Allah has permitted and that khums serves the religious and communal needs of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام and their followers. It also presents payment of khums as a cause of barakah in provision, purification from sins, and a sign of sincere fulfillment of one’s covenant with Allah.
